items.label: section_header
items.text: MAKING PURE SALT FROM ROCK SALT

items.label: text
items.text: Filtration can be used to separate a solid from a liquid.

items.label: text
items.text: For example, sand can be separated from water by filtration. The apparatus for filtration is shown in Figure 2.6.

items.label: text
items.text: The substance left in the filter paper is called the residue and the liquid that comes through is called the filtrate.

items.label: text
items.text: Filtration can also be used to separate two solids from each other if only one of them is soluble in water (see below – rock salt).

items.label: text
items.text: Crystallisation can be used to separate a solute from a solution. For example, it could be used to separate sodium chloride from a sodium chloride solution. The solution is heated in an evaporating basin to boil off some of the water until an almost saturated solution is formed. This can be tested by dipd i g s  ns  oins s   s  onn its surface when it is removed. The Bunsen burner is then turned off and the crystals allowed to form as more water evaporates and the solution cools. The crystals can now be removed from the mixture by filtration.

items.label: text
items.text: The apparatus for crystallisation is shown in Figure 2.7.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 2.7 Crystallisation can be used to separate a solute from a solution.

items.label: text
items.text: We can use filtration and crystallisation to obtain pure salt from rock salt.

items.label: text
items.text: Rock salt consists of salt contaminated by various earthy or rocky impurities. These impurities aren't soluble in water.

items.label: text
items.text: If you crush the rock salt and mix it with hot water, the salt dissolves, but the impurities don't. The impurities can be filtered off, and remain on the filter paper. The filtrate is then a salt solution. The solid salt can be obtained from the solution by crystallisation.

items.label: text
items.text: This is typical of the way you can separate any mixture of two solids, one of which is soluble in water and one of which isn't.
